content.overview: Disposition addresses affected material; CAPA addresses causes and recurrence; change control evaluates planned modifications. Combining them into one undocumented action weakens all three.

vocabulary.definition: Authorized decision about the allowed next state of material.
Structured review, authorization, implementation and verification of a planned change.
Evidence that an action achieved its intended control without unacceptable new effects.

sections.title: Disposition follows evidence and authority
sections.body: Release, rework, rejection or destruction should reference affected scope, evidence and the authorized decision role.

sections.title: CAPA addresses recurrence
sections.body: Actions should correspond to supported causes, have owners and due dates, and be checked for effectiveness.

sections.title: Planned changes are evaluated before routine use
sections.body: Procedure, equipment, packaging or specification changes should consider validation, training, records and downstream impacts.

workedExamples: A packaging seal issue leads to lot disposition, closure-process CAPA and a separately controlled equipment change with verification.
commonMistakes: Using retraining as the default root-cause action.
Changing a process during an investigation without documenting it.
Closing CAPA when implementation is complete but effectiveness is unknown.
content.practicalApplication: Separate one case into disposition, root-cause/CAPA and change-control records with evidence, owners and authorization.
content.summary: Material decisions, recurrence controls and planned changes are linked but require distinct, traceable governance.
